title: Confirm Undo with haptics and warn once when recovery expires
request: Add a haptic when Undo is pressed. User explicitly chose one firm warning cue on expiry, then asked to finish this before the release candidate and push.
expected: Confirm each successful Undo. Request Android's Reject effect once when a live recovery window expires. Paused timers, completed Undo and empty recovery must not produce expiry cues. Respect system Touch feedback and device-supported effects.
approach: Extend the existing AndroidX bridge with Reject and retain its JNI constant through R8. Hook actual recovery actions in View; preserve timing, batching and existing gestures.

regression.tests: UserFlows::test_delete_and_undo_icon and test_undo_expires; test_undo_cancels_expiry_feedback covers touch Undo and absence of a delayed warning, and test_expiry_feedback_waits_for_drawer_close covers pause/resume and one expiry cue. Existing bulk/catalog Undo expectations also require confirmation.
regression.before: With Reject registered but the UI hooks absent, both actual Undo and full 15-second expiry fail: 1 request observed versus 2 expected (out/rc001/undo-haptics-before.txt).
regression.after: Focused suite: 6 records pass, no skips/failures (out/rc001/undo-haptics-final.txt/xml). An initial test-only failure tapped before the popup was open; the fixture now waits for actual removal and popup readiness. The production fix did not change.
regression.limits: Android dispatch uses the existing guarded UI-thread bridge and normal system Touch feedback. Physical feel and older-device fallback remain pending. Semantic Reject requests a firm warning; hardware/settings decide the actual effect. No new dependency, permission or custom vibration waveform.
